title: Drybrushed stone, thinned with tap water
summary: Teaches the blessed pattern for a household diluent: water is declared in paints[] with kind 'additive' and joins the mixture from mix[] at an authored ratio. The additive does not determine the resulting colour, so a colour engine skips it — but its parts are authored data recording the dilution and are never renormalised away.

paints.name: Tap water
paints.note: A household diluent, not a purchasable product: an aggregating consumer must not put this on a shopping list.

steps.instruction: Flood the recesses with Stone Grey thinned heavily with tap water.
steps.mixNote: One part Stone Grey to four parts water.
steps.dryingNotes: Let it dry fully before drybrushing; a damp surface lifts the wash.

steps.instruction: Glaze the flat faces with Stone Grey cut with water and a drop of flow improver.
steps.mixNote: Two parts paint, two parts water, one part flow improver.
steps.expectedResult: An even, slightly translucent grey with no tide marks.

steps.instruction: Drybrush the raised edges with undiluted Stone Grey.
warnings: Wipe the brush almost dry; a loaded brush fills the mortar lines back in.
